themes.consensus_view: Most banks still see the AI spending boom as the main engine lifting stocks and likely to keep going, but a vocal minority warns the trade is dangerously crowded and self-referential, leaving it fragile if AI demand stumbles.

facts_agreed.claim: AI spending and demand remain the dominant driver of equity markets and are seen as more durable than skeptics assume.
evidence_quotes: AI capex can support risk appetite, earnings and parts of global trade for longer than sceptics expect.
underlying measures of AI demand remain firmer than the market reaction suggests
The AI theme continues to drive our outlook for global equity markets.
Our base case remains for this global technology cycle to extend through the rest of the year.

facts_agreed.claim: The next phase of AI spending is broadening beyond GPUs across the wider compute stack, including CPUs and edge hardware.
evidence_quotes: the next phase of AI spend is likely to be distributed more widely across the stack
In the age of AI agents the CPU is now the bottleneck to the GPU.

facts_contested.against_evidence: Momentum Winners are now more long crowded than at any point on record

facts_contested.against_evidence: the positive feedback loop behind AI-linked growth winners can turn

themes.consensus_view: Banks across roughly a dozen research desks flag Middle East conflict, the Israel-Iran-US escalation, and Strait of Hormuz supply risk as a live market driver mainly through oil and energy prices, but none has staked out a clear directional call on where it goes next.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks broadly treat Middle East geopolitical tension as a current macro risk centered on energy and oil supply disruption.
evidence_quotes: Energy price shock from Middle East conflict
Middle East conflict energy price spillover

facts_agreed.claim: Several banks frame the flashpoint specifically as Israel-Iran and US-Iran military escalation, with some watching for de-escalation.

themes.consensus_view: Banks across more than a dozen desks flag a Strait of Hormuz blockade and the resulting oil-flow disruption as a live geopolitical risk to energy markets, but none has yet staked a clear directional call on how it resolves.

facts_agreed.claim: Many banks reference a Strait of Hormuz blockade and oil-flow disruption as an active energy-supply risk this window.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz oil flow disruption

facts_agreed.claim: Banks also frame the Strait of Hormuz situation around its closure, reopening, and knock-on effects for global supply and monetary policy.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz closure impact on global supply
Strait of Hormuz crisis impact on monetary policy
Strait of Hormuz energy export security

themes.consensus_view: Banks expect Japan's central bank to raise interest rates at its June meeting, with Goldman and HSBC both calling a 25 basis point (a quarter of a percent) hike and the rest of the desks treating the move as a live near-term catalyst.

facts_agreed.claim: Both banks staking a view expect the Bank of Japan to raise rates in June.
evidence_quotes: we changed our expectation from a July rate hike to a June rate hike
We expect the BoJ to hike by 25bp at its 16 June meeting

themes.consensus_view: Banks across four desks flag data center buildout as a live theme driving compute, power, and capital spending, but none has staked a directional bet on it yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference the data center buildout as an ongoing growth theme, citing strong demand, an expanding pipeline, and large committed spending.
evidence_quotes: Data center pipeline growth in Europe

themes.consensus_view: Four trading desks flag money moving out of large-cap tech this window through selloffs, de-risking and dispersion, but none has staked a clear directional call on where tech goes next.

facts_agreed.claim: Four banks flag a rotation out of large-cap tech this window through selling, de-risking, and widening performance gaps within the sector.

themes.consensus_view: Four research desks flag US-Iran nuclear negotiations as a live macro watch item, but none has staked out a directional view on whether a deal happens or what it means for markets.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference US-Iran nuclear deal negotiations as an ongoing topic worth tracking, with one tying a potential deal to precious metals.
evidence_quotes: US-Iran deal necessity for precious metals
